tasks.task: Establish site, set up scaffold and access controls
tasks.scope: Site induction, scaffold erection via Kiora Lane and courtyard, edge protection, exclusion zones below active work, resident liaison plan.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold platform collapse or instability during erection
Fall from height — worker fall during scaffold assembly at height >4m
Strike hazard — falling tools or materials from scaffold during erection
Struck by mobile plant — traffic conflict during scaffold delivery via Kiora Lane
Manual handling injury — heavy scaffold components and edge protection panels
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker fall during scaffold assembly at height >4m
controls: Erect scaffold only to design drawings and load plan signed by licensed scaffolder before any component placement starts.
Install edge protection (guardrail and toeboards) on all open edges >4m within 2m of scaffold assembly work.
Establish exclusion zone 5m around base of scaffold during erection; barricade with tape and signs; no resident or unauthorised access.
Wear full-body harness with lanyard clipped to horizontal structural support when working at height >4m; harness inspected before each use.
Tag completed scaffold sections as 'Safe to Use' only after licensed scaffolder checks stability, connections, and handover certificate signed.
Use platform hoists or hand tools only (no dropping); place tools in secured bags when working at height.
Brief all residents on exclusion zones, noise times, and access restrictions before scaffold erection starts; post resident liaison contact on site board.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker onto scaffold platform until: licensed scaffolder has completed handover certificate and site supervisor has signed off scaffold as safe for use.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold connection is loose, damaged, or not matching design detail.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 50 km/h during erection or edge protection is damaged.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker enters exclusion zone without harness and lanyard clipped to approved anchor, or unauthorised resident or vehicle enters zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, and tile bed
tasks.scope: Demolition of failed membrane, screed, and tile bed to all balconies. Dust control and debris removal. Hazardous-material survey and clearance before start.
hazards: Dust inhalation — silica dust and asbestos exposure during membrane and screed breaking
Fall from height — worker positioning on open balcony edge during tile and screed removal
Cut or laceration — sharp edges and fragments from broken tile and concrete
Hazardous material exposure — unconfirmed asbestos in existing membrane or adhesives
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation — asbestos exposure during membrane disturbance
controls: Wet all surfaces with low-pressure water spray before breaking membrane, screed, or tile — keep surfaces visibly damp throughout work.
Use dust extraction with HEPA filter connected to all power tools — cutting, grinding, or chipping must not proceed without active extraction.
Establish exclusion zone on balcony below work area — erect temporary plywood or plastic screen to catch and contain debris.
Wear Type P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted to face — check seal before each use and replace cartridge if breathing resistance increases.
Remove broken tile and screed to sealed waste bags on site — do not sweep or dry-brush broken material.
Check that scaffold is tagged and handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses work area.
check edge protection (guardrail, toe board) on scaffold before each shift — stop work if guardrail is damaged or missing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker on scaffold until: handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and edge protection is verified complete and secure.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails, surfaces become dry, or any area is broken without visible dampness.
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction hose is disconnected, blocked, or HEPA filter is visibly blocked or saturated.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any unknown material (suspected asbestos product, unfamiliar composition) is encountered — re-engage hazmat surveyor before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is damaged, guardrail is loose, or exclusion zone barrier has been breached or removed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: check, document and repair slab cracks and defects
tasks.scope: Crack mapping, substrate assessment, repair of spalling and cracks per engineer direction. Leo and Associates inspection and approval required before membrane application.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker access and movement on open balcony during crack inspection and repair
Struck by falling tools or debris — work at height on exposed slab edge
Dust inhalation — dust generation during crack preparation and grinding
Cut or laceration — sharp concrete edges and abrasive materials during crack repair
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker movement and work on open balcony slab
controls: Verify scaffold erected to engineer specification, load calculations complete, and handover certificate signed before any worker access.
Establish exclusion zone at slab perimeter — minimum 2 m radius below open edge — barricade with tape and signage during entire repair duration.
Wear full body harness with lanyard secured to fixed anchor point before starting crack inspection or repair work on open balcony.
Use wet suppression or local exhaust ventilation during crack grinding, chasing, or surface preparation — no dry breakout allowed.
Check all hand tools and grinders for damage and secure lanyard to harness before use to prevent dropped object strike.
Obtain Leo and Associates inspection sign-off on crack assessment and repair specification before starting repair work.
Conduct pre-start toolbox talk covering hazard identification on open slab, edge proximity, harness attachment points, and rescue procedure.
Stop work and re-brief site if wind gusts exceed 15 m/s or if weather prevents safe harness or adhesive cure conditions.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start repair work until: Leo and Associates has inspected slab, approved repair method and product specification, and signed inspection report.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: all crack repairs are complete, substrate is clean and dry, and Leo and Associates has signed off final condition.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker harness, lanyard, or anchor point is damaged, missing, or not in use during open-slab work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any person enters exclusion zone below open slab edge during active work or tool use.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unknown substrate condition, active water ingress, structural crack pattern, or asbestos-suspected material is discovered during assessment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Obtain and display SDS for crack repair products and adhesive on point of use before application.
Confirm noise management plan in place and occupant notification given before grinding commences.
Record crack mapping, repair method, product used, and Leo and Associates approval in site diary.

Safety helmet with chin strap (mandatory at height)
P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) mask (if dust suppression unavailable)

monitoring.frequency: Before each work session and continuous during active repair
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of harness connection point, lanyard length, and anchor security; supervisor sign-off in site diary.

responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to prepared slab
tasks.scope: Install waterproofing membrane to all balconies and associated slab edges per specification. Full coverage, sealed joints, and edge terminations.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker positioning and movement on balcony edge during membrane installation
Chemical exposure — vapour inhalation from membrane adhesive or primer
Slip hazard — damp or chemical-wet slab surface during membrane application
Thermal burn — contact with heated membrane materials or application equipment
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker movement and access on balcony during membrane installation
controls: Obtain SDS for membrane product and primer. Keep on site and accessible during work. Brief all workers on hazard statements, first aid, and emergency contact before starting.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation across balcony work area. Position fan to direct vapours away from workers and occupied building interior. Check airflow daily before work starts.

check prepared slab surface for contamination, moisture, or loose material. Document substrate condition in writing. Do not apply membrane until substrate is clean, dry, and approved by waterproofing supervisor.
Establish exclusion zone on balcony during membrane application. Restrict access to trained applicators only. Use portable barricade or rope barrier to prevent unplanned pedestrian entry.
Lay down anti-slip matting or temporary surface protection across the working area before chemical application. Replace or move as membrane cures to maintain safe foot contact.

Keep application equipment (heated membrane applicators, torch, rollers) staged at least 2 m from balcony edge. Designate a cool-down station away from the working edge. Never leave heated equipment unattended on the slab.

Wear chemical-resistant gloves and chemical-resistant apron during all primer and adhesive application. Change gloves immediately if torn or contaminated. Remove PPE only after washing hands and exposed skin with soap and water.

Wear P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) during primer application and first-coat membrane laying. Verify mask fits correctly and is undamaged before starting. Replace mask if it becomes damp or damaged during work.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: Waterproofing supervisor inspects and signs off substrate condition in writing, including confirmation of cleanliness, dryness, and surface preparation compliance.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to joint sealing and edge termination until: First coat membrane has fully cured per SDS cure time and product manufacturer's written instruction.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Continuous mechanical ventilation fails or is disabled, or airflow direction cannot be maintained toward exterior.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Worker experiences respiratory irritation, dizziness, or nausea during chemical application or primer work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Substrate becomes wet, contaminated, or damaged before or during membrane application, or if unexpected substrate material is discovered.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Keep SDS and product technical data on file and accessible at the work site throughout application and curing period.

Establish emergency contact procedure for chemical exposure. make sure first aid kit includes eye wash, activated charcoal (if SDS specifies), and burn treatment. Confirm nearest hospital and emergency protocols with site supervisor before starting.

Steel-capped boots with good grip and oil-resistant sole
High-visibility vest (day) or reflective clothing (night work, if applicable)

monitoring.frequency: Before work starts each day; continuously during application
monitoring.evidence: Visual observation of fan operation and airflow direction; weather log; substrate inspection sign-off sheet; SDS on-site checklist

responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply new waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

tasks.task: Prepare substrate: clean, prime and level slab surface
tasks.scope: Remove debris, clean slab, apply primer and levelling compound where required. Substrate hold point confirmation by Leo and Associates before membrane application.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker positioning and movement on balcony edge during cleaning and priming
Chemical exposure — vapour inhalation from primer and levelling compound application
Slip hazard — wet/damp slab surface during priming and cleaning
Eye irritation or chemical burn — splash from primer or levelling compound
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker movement and access on balcony during surface preparation
controls: Install edge protection (guardrail or safety net) along balcony edge before cleaning starts. Edge protection must be certified compliant and inspected daily.
Wear full-body harness with lanyard secured to fixed anchor point during all work within 2m of edge. Anchor point must be load-tested and certified.
Obtain and read SDS for primer and levelling compound on point of use before opening containers.
Ventilate balcony area continuously during primer and levelling compound application. Open windows and position portable fan to direct vapour away from workers and occupied spaces.
Apply primer and levelling compound only when weather permits (no rain, wind <20 km/h, air temperature 10–25°C). Check weather forecast before starting.
Lay absorbent mat or cloth over cleaned slab to prevent slipping during priming. Replace mat if saturated.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves (nitrile minimum), eye protection, and hi-viz shirt or vest
Confine primer and levelling compound spills to small containers with drip trays. Do not pour or dispose into stormwater. Sweep and contain spilt powder before wet cleaning.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer or levelling compound until: Leo and Associates confirms substrate is clean, dry, and levelling requirement assessed. Confirmation must be signed and dated on site.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to membrane application until: Leo and Associates inspects and signs off primed and levelled slab surface. Acceptance signed on site before waterproofing membranes are opened.

🛑 STOP WORK if: wind exceeds 20 km/h, rain begins, or air temperature falls below 10°C or exceeds 25°C — primer cure window cannot be met.
🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fan fails, vapour odour becomes strong, or worker reports dizziness, headache, or respiratory discomfort.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Install screed layer and allow cure time
tasks.scope: Lay and finish screed bed over membrane. Cure time observed and protective covering maintained.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker positioning during screed installation on balcony slab
Slip hazard — fresh screed surface during laying and finishing
Manual handling injury — screed material mixing and placement
Thermal burn — contact with fresh cement screed or heated materials
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker movement and access on balcony during screed installation
controls: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder and retained on site before any worker accesses scaffold.
Verify edge protection installed — guardrail minimum 1.0 m high, mid-rail at 0.5 m, toe-board 0.15 m — at all open edges of balcony slab before screed work starts.
Wear full harness with lanyard clipped to certified anchor point during all screed laying and finishing work.
Lay screed only during daylight or with task lighting that eliminates shadows on work surface and edge detection.
Establish wet zone exclusion area — barricade and delineate all wet screed surface with hazard tape and warning signs; no pedestrian access permitted during laying and initial set.
Wet-check all screed material before laying — confirm moisture content and workability per membrane product SDS; reject material if storage, mixing, or transport conditions not met.
Maintain protective covering over screed cure period — cover with plastic sheeting or tarps; secure to prevent wind displacement or trip hazard; maintain for full cure time specified in membrane SDS.
Brief all workers before start — confirm harness use, anchor points, edge protection location, wet zone, and cure schedule; obtain verbal acknowledgement from each worker.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lay screed until: scaffold handover certificate is signed and site-retained, edge protection is installed and checked, and weather window is confirmed for cure period.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove protective covering until: cure time specified in membrane SDS has elapsed and site supervisor has visually confirmed full set of screed bed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker is observed working at height without harness clipped to anchor point.
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is damaged, incomplete, or temporarily removed without documented replacement.
🛑 STOP WORK if: protective covering is displaced, torn, or breached during cure period, or if cure time cannot be maintained due to weather or access pressure.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tell building occupants of cure period and exclusion zone — maintain notification visible for duration of cure time.

High-visibility vest or shirt — class D compliant; worn by all workers.
eye protection— impact-rated; worn when mixing or handling dry screed material.

tasks.task: Lay tiles and reinstate balustrades and fittings
tasks.scope: Install tiles to screed. Reinstate balustrades, handrails, and associated fittings. Grout and seal all joints.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker access on balcony edge during tile laying and balustrade reinstallation
Struck by falling balustrade or handrail components — during installation of edge protection
Cut or laceration — sharp tile edges and grout handling
Slip hazard — grouting process and residual slurry on finished surface
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker access and movement on balcony during tile and balustrade work
controls: Erect and tag scaffold before any worker accesses balcony. Verify handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before use.
Wear full-body harness and lanyard clipped to named anchor point on scaffold frame during all elevated work.
Install edge protection (guardrail minimum 1.1m high) on scaffold working platform. Check daily for damage or displacement.
Lay tiles on prepared screed only. Stop work if screed surface is uneven, wet, or contaminated.
Handle cut tiles wearing cut-resistant gloves and eye protection
Mix and apply grout per product SDS. Ventilate grouting area continuously. No grouting in rain or below 5°C.
Barricade grouted balcony edge with hazard tape and 'Slippery' signs during cure. Prohibit worker access until grout cures.
Reinstate balustrades and handrails using named fixings per engineer detail. Verify installation with torque wrench before load test.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not lay tiles until: screed inspection signed off by site supervisor and surface defects remedied
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not reinstate balustrades until: tile and grout cure confirmed and balcony surface is stable
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: harness or lanyard fails, anchor point is compromised, or edge protection is damaged
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions prevent grouting (rain, temperature below 5°C, or wind exceeds 40 km/h)
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed is uneven, wet, or contaminated, or balustrade fixings cannot be installed to engineer detail
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Lanyard with energy absorber (1.8m maximum free fall)

Slip hazard — grouted tile surface during final walkover
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — inspector movement on open balcony slab
controls: Wear full body harness with shock absorber attached to certified anchor point before stepping onto balcony slab.
Install temporary edge protection — 1.1m high barrier rail — along all open edges before inspection starts.
Check balcony slab surface for grout smears and loose debris; damp-wipe tiles and allow 30 min cure before walking.
Limit inspector movement to marked safe path; prohibit solo inspection — second person must remain in constant visual contact.
Stop work if wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or if any edge protection is incomplete, loose, or damaged.
Remove all tools, materials, and debris from balcony slab before final walkover.
Conduct defects identification in daylight only; use torchlight for shadows — do not lean over edges.
Photograph all defects and record location on defect register before any rectification work begins.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start inspector walkover until: temporary edge protection installed, harness anchor point certified, and site induction confirms fall-arrest procedure.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not sign final defect list until: Leo and Associates approves all defect locations and remedial scope in writing.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h, edge protection is damaged or incomplete, or harness becomes detached.
🛑 STOP WORK if: slip hazard on tile surface cannot be eliminated by damp-wiping, or unknown substrate condition is encountered.
🛑 STOP WORK if: inspector loses visual contact with safety observer, or solo inspection occurs.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — worker access and movement during scaffold dismantling at height >4m
Struck by falling scaffold components — platform sections or tubes during deconstruction
Struck by mobile plant — debris removal traffic via Kiora Lane
Manual handling injury — heavy scaffold components and edge protection removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker fall during scaffold dismantling at height >4m
controls: Obtain signed scaffold handover certificate and load calculations from licenced scaffolder before any dismantling task starts.
Establish exclusion zone minimum 2m beyond scaffold perimeter on ground level. Barricade with physical barrier and warning signs. No pedestrian or vehicle access permitted.
Wear full body harness with lanyard clipped to independent anchor point during all work at height >2m. Anchor points checked and certified before first use each day.
Dismantle scaffold from top down in planned sequence. Remove only sections that do not compromise structural stability of remaining scaffold.
Lower all scaffold tubes, platform sections, and edge protection to ground via controlled descent or lowering equipment. No free-dropping or throwing of components.
check each scaffold section before removal for damage, cracks, or instability. Do not remove components showing defects — mark and report to supervisor.
Brief all workers on exclusion zone boundaries and no-go areas before work starts. Nominate a ground spotter to monitor exclusion zone throughout dismantling.
Use mobile elevated work platform (MEWP) or mobile scaffold tower only if ground conditions and access permit. Do not use on slopes, soft ground, or uneven surfaces.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any scaffold dismantling until: Licenced scaffolder has signed scaffold handover certificate and load calculations, all workers have current White Card and Working at Heights competency verification, and exclusion zone is fully established with physical barriers and signage in place.

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove final edge protection or guard rails until: Supervisor has confirmed all personnel have exited elevated areas and exclusion zone is secure with no pedestrian or vehicle traffic.
